notes.title: SOLAS 128 Accessibilty Update and 34% Off Sale
notes.content:
Hey all, Tom here!

Big news today, as not only is there a huge SOLAS 128 Accessibility update, but also a sale to celebrate Global Accessibility Awareness Day!

As some of you might be aware, accessibility has been a core part of the design of SOLAS 128 from the start. The coloured glyphs are designed to help those with colour-blindness be able to play the game, for example. But I was aware it wasn't perfect. Since launch we've had fantastic feedback and suggestions from players and accessibility experts, and I've been working on a big update to make the game even more customisable!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37692459/04edff6a34c31cef0be16149fd3ec5b2bd881ea4.jpg[/img]

Once updated, players will find a whole new menu of options full of player-requested options like being able to tweak the bloom or colour distortion amount, or even an entirely new input method for those who struggle to hold down buttons. Keyboard input has also been massively improved, to allow more accurate movement with the cursor/WASD keys, and a new hotkeys have been added to skip straight to the next or previous piece you can interact with.

[b] If you're not sure, please do try out the demo/prologue first, as I've updated it as well, to made sure all the same options are available. If you can customise the demo to work for you, you'll be able to customise the full game too![/b]

For a full list of new features/updates see below, but I really hope these updates help!

-Amicable Animal

[h2]New Features[/h2]
[h3]Visual Options (for visual processing accessibility)[/h3]
[olist]
[*] Settings for the bloom/glow effect (original, low, off)
[*] Settings for colour distortion/chromic aberration (original, low, off)
[*] Option for the VHS-style video distortion effects (on, off)
[*] Settings to simplify the game's surrounding border pattern (original, static, solid colour)
[*] Option for the 'flashing' effect in the surrounding pattern (on, off)
[/olist]
[h3]Input Options (for motor accessibility)[/h3]
[olist]
[*] New input type - original input is click & drag, new option removes requirement to hold down a button while dragging. One click to pick up, a second to put down
[*] New optional precision input method - directional keys (d-pad on Switch) will move the cursor locked to the game's tile grid, rather than as a smooth input.
[*] Can either be depressed once per tile, or held down as desired
[*] Analogue/mouse and precision input can be swapped between freely and used at the same time
[*] New selection method - Next/Previous selection option lets players with visual processing issues or motor issues cycle through selectable pieces.
[/olist]
[h3]Bug Fixes[/h3]
[olist]
[*] Filters will now check and reactive if necessarily when you change screen
[*] 'Invalid' spaces should appear more obvious now
[*] Lots of other tiny fixes
[/olist]

notes.title: SOLAS 128 Patch Notes - v1.02
notes.content:
Hello everyone! 

Today's SOLAS 128 update addresses a couple bugs and strange behaviors reported since the game launched.  If you've been enjoying the game please be sure to leave a review here on Steam, it's a great way to continue to support the game.   You can find the full details of the patch below.  



[b]SOLAS 128  v1.02 Changelog[/b]
[list]
[*] Penultimate cutscene should no longer softlock the game if the mirrors have already been removed
[*] Players should no longer be able to 'fast forward' through the game outro
[*] Flip mirrors should be much less likely to change orientation when the game is saving, so older areas shouldn't need to be rewired
[*] Pulse doors should no longer get out of sync if they are transitioning during a save/screen move/quit action
[*] A pulse button in the red area should no longer affect a pulse door in the green area (starting from a new save required)
[*] Filter emitters should now act as walls for the pulses, rather than mirrors – pulses can no longer 'escape' the world through them later in the game and cause issues. 
[/list]

notes.title: The 29 Languages
notes.content:
こんにちは | Cześć | Hello!

Today I'm delighted to announce that SOLAS 128 will support in-game translations for all 29 languages that Steam supports! See the video below for how this works.

[previewyoutube=ZQePodgEarg;full][/previewyoutube]

Originally SOLAS 128 was going to have no words within it, but after our first round of beta testing we realised players struggled to navigate the settings menu. notes.title: SOLAS is in the Steam Game Festival!
notes.content:
At its heart, SOLAS is a beam deflection puzzle game inspired by games like Deflektor, The Witness, Rez, and Tetris Effect. 

Players can move and rotate mirrors which will redirect light. Unlike other games in this genre, however, the light is not a continuous beam, but instead made of discrete pulses that can collide, combine, and deflect each other. This means that the underlying beat of the game becomes a vital component, as puzzles are often based around timing pulses to either avoid or hit each other.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37692459/80f51ea96e454d39148d588e4f8c167c85b2b06e.gif[/img]

The game is made up of a single, constantly simulated, seamless world. Initial pulses emitted from the logo flow through every puzzle in the game and each room solved serves as a smaller piece of a greater whole. Every gate opened unlocks new paths to explore. 

The SOLAS Prologue is a small selection of levels built specially for this release, designed to sample what makes SOLAS unique.

notes.title: The Origins of SOLAS
notes.content:
Hello everyone! I'm Tom, usually known as Amicable Animal, and I wanted to welcome you to the first post on this (almost) brand new Steam page! I'm hugely excited to be writing this after a year's worth of work on SOLAS. 

I thought it would be nice to give a bit of background for this first post – SOLAS's origin story, if you will. So here goes: SOLAS is a game born out of 2019's Global Game Jam. I met Steven and Jamesy (the sound designer and musician working with me) in those panicked 48 hours and convinced them to work with me on a rhythm-based Tetris/Puyo Puyo like game called HJEM (which you can play right now, incidentally). We liked working together enough that when I had an idea for a more sprawling, complex puzzle game that ran on music, they agreed to help me realise it!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37692459/80f51ea96e454d39148d588e4f8c167c85b2b06e.gif[/img]

But what started as a weird little idea that I wasn't sure would even work, soon grew into this interconnected world of strange glyphs and neon clockwork you see here... and I couldn't be happier! 

SOLAS is inspired by the C64/Spectrum and Flash games that I grew up on. The game design is influenced by classic games like Deflektor and older single-screen dungeon crawler games, as well as more modern titles like The Witness. The interconnectedness of the puzzles even reflects my love for classic Zelda dungeons! Those influences, combined with a good few twists and ideas of my own, lead to a game that is a pretty unique puzzle experience!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/37692459/de03556fe1c0175290d36a25a3692f96f5725716.png[/img]

In particular, it is designed to be a game about observation and internalisation – a game where solutions to puzzles might pop into your head while you are washing up or taking a walk. For the music and visuals, artists like Daft Punk, GUNSHIP, and Lane 8 have also helped inspire the strange, bloom-filled world.

I really can't wait for you to play it! Until then, I hope you enjoy the trailer and the screenshots. Oh, and if you haven't already, please consider wishlisting SOLAS. Not only does it really help, but it will keep you up to date with any exciting upcoming announcements!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1257850/SOLAS/

Amicable Animal
